title: The Log Is The Agent - Ishaan Sehgal, Omnara
talk_summary: Ishaan Sehgal argues the durable append-only event log, not the model or runtime, is the agent's identity; workers are disposable executors that reconstruct state from the log, advance one step, and append results. This makes reliability, failover, forking, migration, and multi-agent sharing structural properties rather than bolted-on features.

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat the append-only event log as the durable agent state; any worker can claim a session, reconstruct state from the log, advance one step, append the result, and disappear.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A worker can claim the session, read the log, advance the agent one step, write the result, and then just completely disappear.

takeaways.what_they_do: Because the log holds pending permission prompts and state transitions, a new worker reconstructs the session and finds the prompt exactly where it was, instead of the agent being paused or losing the prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the permission prompt will be gone, and the agent will be paused. And that is unacceptable in production.

takeaways.technique: Compaction as lossy projection, keep raw log
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you keep the raw log, you can always generate new projections from it. But if you throw away the raw log and keep only the compaction, you've effectively lost part of the agent.
One branch can run on Claude, another branch can run on GPT, another can run on your favorite open-source model.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one process per agent, workers reconstruct state from the log each turn, so one process can advance thousands of agents with no sticky sessions or state migration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: One process can now advance thousands of agents. Each of them can reconstruct their state from the log on each turn

takeaways.technique: Own the log to avoid lock-in
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the session log in infrastructure you control and queryable by you, since provider-owned logs are the deepest form of lock-in; migration becomes an adapter problem over projections.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The deepest form of lock-in is actually log lock-in. If a provider owns your log, then the provider effectively owns your agent
